key_insight: Reward models inherit value and representational biases from their LLM pretraining seeds, producing systematic, model-specific preference patterns across psycholinguistic and demographic dimensions.
problem_solved: Identifies and characterizes how pretraining representations shape downstream reward-model behavior and value judgments—an understudied source of alignment bias that can undermine RLHF and evaluation pipelines.
method: Compare 10 open-weight reward models initialized from different pretrained LLMs using validated psycholinguistic corpora and demographic stimuli.
Measure and statistically test RM preference patterns across multiple semantic and social dimensions to detect systematic biases.
Analyze how initialization history and representational features correlate with observed value shifts in reward outputs.
impact: Highlights a hidden pathway for bias transfer into alignment components: practitioners must audit RM initialization and incorporate mitigation strategies (dataset design, calibration, alternative fine-tuning) to ensure more robust, value-aligned systems.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing inheritance: Pretrained LLM → RM initialization → RM scoring behavior (labels: representations, fine-tuning, reward outputs).
Heatmap comparing bias magnitude across 10 RMs and multiple psycholinguistic/demographic dimensions.
Bar/violin plots showing distribution of preference scores for representative stimuli (e.g., neutral vs. value-laden prompts).
Checklist/decision flow for practitioners (audit steps, mitigation options, monitoring) with icons for data, model, and evaluation.
paper_title: Reward Models Inherit Value Biases from Pretraining
paper_authors: Brian Christian, Jessica A. F. Thompson, Elle Michelle Yang, Vincent Adam, Hannah Rose Kirk
